instruction: This is a HANDOFF, not outreach execution. All 20 candidates below were found via live web search tonight and spot-checked (3 of 20, one per angle-type) to confirm they are real, currently-published pages -- not invented URLs.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: Names Intercom Fin's $0.99/resolution model as the template for outcome-based AI pricing.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: Reports Intercom Fin's $0.99/resolution rate and argues outcome-based pricing captures 20-30% of delivered value vs 10-15% for subscription SaaS.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.idealDeepLink: Cite alongside the benchmark's own Intercom row as independent corroboration.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: Survey data showing the seat+AI-usage hybrid trend is industry-wide, not CS-specific.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: 37% of ~230 surveyed B2B companies now use hybrid seat+consumption pricing; 29% sell AI credits today.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.idealDeepLink: Use to frame the benchmark's 9-of-16 finding as part of a broader trend.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: Already lines up HubSpot, Intercom, Zendesk, Salesforce on per-resolution rates -- a near-miniature version of the benchmark.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: HubSpot Breeze moved from $1.00 to $0.50/resolved conversation (April 2026); Intercom Fin $0.99/resolution at 66-67% average resolution rate.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.idealDeepLink: Natural cross-reference for the benchmark's own methodology section.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: Finance-side rationale for reporting seat revenue separately from usage revenue.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: Argues ARR should separate usage-based from fixed seat-based revenue given differing predictability.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.idealDeepLink: Supports the benchmark's own seat-vs-usage separation methodology.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: Billing-infrastructure vendor's explanation of why AI compute costs push hybrid pricing.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: AI's per-inference costs are pushing vendors toward hybrid subscription+usage models.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.idealDeepLink: Framing citation for why AI-usage pricing is emerging as a category.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: Defines Cost Per Resolution as the standard unit-economics metric for AI support spend.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: Defines CPR as spend-per-fully-resolved-issue, the same normalization the benchmark uses.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.idealDeepLink: Cite in the benchmark's methodology section on why per-resolution is the comparison unit.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: First-party explanation of Intercom's own outcome-based pricing philosophy.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: Describes extending the $0.99/resolution model from support to sales.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.idealDeepLink: Primary-source corroboration for the benchmark's Intercom row.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: Gorgias's own explainer of its metered AI Agent add-on pricing.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: ~$1.00/resolved interaction monthly (~$0.90 annual), overage ~$1.50 each, double-meters against the base ticket allowance.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.idealDeepLink: Corroborates and adds nuance to the benchmark's Gorgias row.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: A competing market-wide AI-support pricing benchmark -- closest existing analog to Miloosh's own asset.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: Catalogs 4 coexisting pricing models and benchmarks named vendors' per-resolution rates.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.idealDeepLink: Candidate for a comparison callout or corroborating citation in the benchmark's own text.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: CX-leadership publication writing for the same buyer persona the benchmark targets.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: Practical framework for CX leaders piloting agentic AI.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.idealDeepLink: Candidate for a 'how to use this benchmark' framing section.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: Real product company blog making unsourced total-cost claims Miloosh's benchmark could substantiate.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: Calculates a 10-agent Freshdesk team's real cost at ~$627/mo once AI add-ons are included.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.idealDeepLink: Candidate to cite Miloosh's benchmark as the sourced backing.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: Established vendor comparison guide across 11 platforms.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: Flat $29/agent pricing claim contrasted against Zendesk's $115/agent.

forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.whyRelevant: Established ITSM company blog with a dated 10-vendor pricing comparison.
forCustomerSupportPricingBenchmark.exactFinding: Zoho Desk Express at $7/agent as cheapest; Salesforce Service Cloud up to $350/user/month.

forCrmPlanGateDataset.whyRelevant: A dedicated CRM feature-gating piece with unsourced tier claims -- exact topic match.
forCrmPlanGateDataset.exactFinding: Names HubSpot's Starter automation gate and Salesforce's Enterprise forecasting gate with no cited source.
forCrmPlanGateDataset.idealDeepLink: Strongest single candidate to pitch a citation to Miloosh's dataset as the sourced backing.

forCrmPlanGateDataset.whyRelevant: Canonical CRM-shopping resource; breaks tiers into entry/mid/high with feature gates.
forCrmPlanGateDataset.exactFinding: Entry tiers ($34.77/user avg) exclude email automation; mid-tier ($64.58/user avg) adds it.
forCrmPlanGateDataset.idealDeepLink: Candidate citation in its tier-comparison section.

forCrmPlanGateDataset.whyRelevant: Sales-ops comparison built around exactly Miloosh's question (which tier unlocks sync/sequences).
forCrmPlanGateDataset.exactFinding: States Pipedrive Growth is where full sync/automation/sequences unlock.
forCrmPlanGateDataset.idealDeepLink: Candidate for per-vendor pricing subsection citation.

forCrmPlanGateDataset.whyRelevant: Reviews 7 CRM/sales platforms with pricing + automation features side by side.
forCrmPlanGateDataset.exactFinding: Lists per-vendor entry pricing and calls out Freshsales/Close automation features.
forCrmPlanGateDataset.idealDeepLink: Candidate citation in its numbered tool sections.

forCrmPlanGateDataset.whyRelevant: CRM-switcher-focused content naming HubSpot's free-tier limitations.
forCrmPlanGateDataset.exactFinding: States follow-up visibility is 'available at paid tiers' on HubSpot.
forCrmPlanGateDataset.idealDeepLink: Candidate citation in its comparison table.

forCrmPlanGateDataset.whyRelevant: Vendor content-marketing piece on CRM hidden fees and tier gating.
forCrmPlanGateDataset.exactFinding: Claims automation limits are deliberately set low on starter tiers.

linkEarningCandidates.note: 20 candidates total requested; 18 returned strong matches across the two assets. 2 of the 4 'general roundup' angle candidates (Drag, HelpSpot, InvGate) doubled as customer-support-benchmark matches and are listed once above under that asset rather than duplicated.

cmsBuyingDecisionMatrixLinkableFindings.releaseCorrection: Codex first-party recheck 2026-09-27 supersedes the original lock-in claims. Deployment verification is recorded in ../20260927-cms-release/deployment.json; do not pitch until that receipt confirms live.
strongDefensibleFindings: Seven of eight sampled platforms have documented content-input and content-output mechanisms under the explicitly broad file/API/same-platform transfer definition
Webflow CMS supports CSV import and export; arbitrary website-code import is a different question
Export files, API extraction and complete-site migration are not interchangeable; schemas, media and application behavior need validation
limitations: 'Documented' is not the same as 'complete' -- several import tools are limited to specific source platforms (e.g. WordPress-only importers)
Official documentation subdomains are first-party sources. Webflow and Contentful bot/rate responses were resolved by read-only live browser verification; no bypass used
This is a dated snapshot (2026-09-27) of documentation, not of actual migration difficulty in practice
audienceAngles: Web agencies and freelance developers evaluating a CMS for a client -- the migration-direction framing is a real risk-disclosure question they should be asking vendors
Enterprise buyers doing CMS RFPs -- hosting and documented transfer boundaries are due-diligence inputs; most commercial-support terms remain unassessed
CMS implementers -- validate the documented formats against a real destination content model
claimsThatMustNotBeMade: Do NOT present this as a ranking of which CMS is 'best' -- it computes no score
Do NOT repeat the superseded WordPress-only, Webflow-no-import, or no-export claims for Craft, Drupal, Contentful or Storyblok
Do NOT quote support prices or SLAs from this research; they are deliberately not measured

pitchPackForCmsAsset.webDevelopersAgencies: Lead with the migration-lock-in framing -- a real risk-disclosure angle agencies should raise with clients before recommending a CMS.
pitchPackForCmsAsset.enterpriseBuyers: Lead with hosting choices, documented transfer scope and unanswered support questions as RFP inputs, not a verified support-price comparison.
pitchPackForCmsAsset.cmsVendorsThemselves: Lead with an invitation to correct the record via the Corrections Policy if a documented export path exists that this research missed.
